instructional_objects.definition: An account of how and why one condition, event, or process contributes to another.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Explain the mechanism by which one thing produces another.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Identify the proposed cause and outcome; explain the mechanism connecting them; consider contributing conditions, alternative causes, sequence, and evidence; avoid confusing correlation with causation.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Is causation asserted without a mechanism? Are multiple causes reduced to one? Could the relationship be reversed, coincidental, or mediated by another factor?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Causation asserted without mechanism; multiple causes reduced to one; correlation mistaken for causation.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask, “By what process would this produce that result?” Help the student identify intermediate steps and competing explanations.

instructional_objects.definition: The organization of examples into meaningful groups based on shared criteria.

instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Are categories based on one clear principle? Do they overlap unnecessarily? Are important cases omitted or forced into unsuitable groups?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Inconsistent grouping principle; overlapping categories; forced or omitted cases.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask what feature is being used to sort the examples and whether that feature is applied consistently to every case.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_control: The student creates purposeful, coherent categories and revises them when examples reveal ambiguity or overlap.

instructional_objects.writer_function: Requires the writer to choose one grouping criterion and apply it consistently.

functional_relationships.reader: Lets the reader see how many cases are organized and why.

functional_relationships.overall_organization: Structured by one criterion; overlap and borderline cases addressed.

productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner is organizing material.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Introduce a single consistent criterion applied to every case.

productive_misconceptions.leverage: Tie categories to purpose; address borderline cases honestly.

indicators_of_development.flexible: The student creates purposeful, coherent categories and revises them when examples reveal ambiguity or overlap.

recognition_diagnostics_detailed.next_move: Ask what feature sorts the examples and whether it is applied consistently to every case.

instructional_objects.definition: Language or structure that helps readers understand how one idea, sentence, paragraph, or section relates to another.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Show the reader the real relationship between ideas.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Determine the actual relationship between ideas; express that relationship through wording, repetition, sentence structure, or sequencing; provide enough guidance without mechanical labeling.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Can the reader follow the shift? Is the relationship additive, contrasting, causal, sequential, illustrative, or concessive? Is the transition word inaccurate or superficial?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Reader can't follow the shift; transition word inaccurate or superficial; mechanical labeling.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask the student to state the relationship between the two ideas in ordinary language, then express that relationship in the writing.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_control: The student creates transitions based on genuine conceptual relationships and uses them flexibly without relying on a stock list.
instructional_objects.reader_function: Helps the reader see how one idea, sentence, paragraph, or section relates to another.
instructional_objects.writer_function: Requires the writer to name the real relationship first, then express it — not paste a connective.

functional_relationships.purpose: Transitions serve coherence by making relationships between ideas visible.
functional_relationships.reader: Signals the relationship (add/contrast/cause/sequence/illustrate/concede) so the reader can follow the shift.
functional_relationships.neighboring_components: Realizes Coherence; connects Paragraphs and Sentences; supports Organization.
functional_relationships.overall_organization: Placed at each shift the reader must track; flexible, not a stock list.

common_difficulties.description: The connective names a relationship the ideas do not actually have.
A transition word is added without a real conceptual link.
A shift occurs with no signal, so the reader cannot follow it.
Stock connectives are applied by formula rather than to the relationship.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: Transitions mean words like 'however' and 'therefore'.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner knows connectives help.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Move from vocabulary to relationship: name the link, then express it (with words, repetition, or structure).

productive_misconceptions.misconception: Every sentence needs a transition word.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner attends to flow.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Focus on genuine shifts the reader must track.

indicators_of_development.early: Adds or omits connectives without identifying the real relationship between ideas.
indicators_of_development.partial: Signals relationships in places but some are inaccurate or superficial; corrects when the relationship is stated in plain words first.
indicators_of_development.independent: The student creates transitions based on genuine conceptual relationships and uses them flexibly without relying on a stock list.
indicators_of_development.flexible: The student creates transitions based on genuine conceptual relationships and uses them flexibly without relying on a stock list.

recognition_diagnostics_detailed.attempting: Is the learner naming the relationship or pasting a connective? Quote the transition.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.control_level: Accurate relationship, expressed flexibly, reader can follow the shift? Map to levels.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.likely_misconception: Word without link -> superficial; wrong connective -> inaccurate.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.next_move: Ask the learner to state the relationship between the two ideas in ordinary language, then express it in the writing.

developmental_invitations.use_when: A shift is unsignaled or mislabeled.

instructional_objects.definition: A sentence that identifies the central contribution a paragraph makes to the surrounding discussion.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Tell the reader the single contribution the paragraph makes and connect it to the thesis.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Establish the paragraph’s focus; state or imply its principal claim or function; connect it to the thesis or preceding discussion; prepare the reader for the paragraph’s development.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Does the sentence merely announce a topic? Does it accurately represent the paragraph? Is the paragraph’s contribution clear without it?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Merely announces a topic; doesn't represent the paragraph; no clear contribution.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask, “What single idea does this paragraph help the reader understand?” Help the student state that idea in relation to the larger argument.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_control: Topic sentences increasingly express meaningful claims, orient the reader, and accurately govern paragraph development.
instructional_objects.reader_function: Tells the reader the one contribution this paragraph makes, so they know how to read what follows and how it advances the whole.
instructional_objects.writer_function: Commits the writer to a single paragraph job and gives a test for what belongs in the paragraph.

functional_relationships.purpose: Names the paragraph's share of the whole purpose; if the paragraph's job is unclear, the topic sentence is where it must be decided.
functional_relationships.reader: Orients the reader to the paragraph's point before its development; without it the reader must guess.
functional_relationships.neighboring_components: Advances one part of the Thesis; governs the Supporting Detail and Concluding Sentence beneath it.
functional_relationships.overall_organization: Each topic sentence should trace to some part of the controlling idea; sequence of topic sentences reveals the essay's organization.

common_difficulties.description: Announces a subject ('This paragraph is about X') without stating the paragraph's contribution.
Promises something the paragraph does not actually develop.
The paragraph's point is already clear, so a stated topic sentence adds nothing.
States a point unrelated to the thesis or the preceding discussion.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: Every paragraph must start with a topic sentence.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: Shows awareness that paragraphs need a governing point.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Move from placement to function: the point may be stated or implied, as long as one contribution governs the paragraph.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: A topic sentence just names the paragraph's topic.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner can locate the subject.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Push from topic to contribution: what does this paragraph help the reader understand about the thesis?

indicators_of_development.early: Announces a topic or restates the thesis; cannot say what the paragraph contributes.
indicators_of_development.partial: States a real contribution but it drifts from the paragraph's actual development or from the thesis; revises when shown the mismatch.
indicators_of_development.independent: Topic sentences increasingly express meaningful claims, orient the reader, and accurately govern paragraph development.
indicators_of_development.flexible: Topic sentences increasingly express meaningful claims, orient the reader, and accurately govern paragraph development.

recognition_diagnostics_detailed.attempting: Is the learner naming a topic, restating the thesis, or asserting the paragraph's contribution? Quote the candidate sentence.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.control_level: Does it express a meaningful claim/function, orient the reader, and match what the paragraph develops? Map to early/partial/independent/flexible.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.likely_misconception: Only names a subject -> topic_not_claim; promises more than the paragraph delivers -> inaccurate.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.next_move: Ask what single idea the paragraph helps the reader understand, then align the sentence to the paragraph's real work.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Surface the single idea the paragraph contributes.
developmental_invitations.use_when: The sentence only names a topic.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Tie the paragraph's point to the thesis.
developmental_invitations.use_when: The paragraph feels unrelated to the argument.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Align the sentence to what the paragraph actually develops.
Have the learner state the paragraph's job in their own words.
developmental_invitations.avoid_when: The learner is still unclear on the concept.

followup_decisions.after: The topic sentence now works but a neighbor is the real obstacle.

followup_decisions.consider: conclude this target — consolidate and release.

followup_decisions.after: Learner asks to proceed on their own.

Re-derive the sentence from what the paragraph actually proves, then align the two.
Cut a topic sentence that only labels the subject if the paragraph's point is already clear.
stopping_conditions: Learner independently produces a topic sentence that performs its canonical function for this reader and purpose.
Diminishing returns — the element substantially works and further tuning yields little developmental gain.
Another component has become the primary obstacle to communicating the meaning.
Learner requests independence.
Teacher override designates a different focus.

transfer.other_disciplines: Lab and history writing still need each section's contribution made visible.
transfer.future_writing: Foundational for structuring reports, memos, and proposals a reader can skim by leads.

instructional_objects.definition: Specific information that develops, clarifies, illustrates, or supports a paragraph’s central idea.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Develop a paragraph's claim with functionally relevant specifics.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Determine what the paragraph’s claim requires; add relevant facts, examples, descriptions, quotations, or reasoning; explain their relationship to the central idea.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Is the paragraph underdeveloped? Are details relevant, sufficient, and ordered? Do they support the main idea or merely concern the same topic?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Underdeveloped; details merely on-topic rather than supporting the point; poorly ordered.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask what the reader still needs to know or understand to accept the paragraph’s main point.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_control: The student selects and organizes details according to their function rather than accumulating loosely related information.
instructional_objects.reader_function: Gives the reader concrete grounds to understand or accept the paragraph's point, not just more words on the topic.
instructional_objects.writer_function: Forces the writer to decide what the claim actually requires and to make each detail earn its place.

functional_relationships.purpose: Serves the paragraph's contribution; details that do not develop the point do not serve the purpose.
functional_relationships.reader: Supplies what the reader still needs to understand or believe the point.
functional_relationships.neighboring_components: Develops the Topic Sentence; overlaps Evidence and Example as the material a paragraph uses.
functional_relationships.overall_organization: Ordered by function within the paragraph, not by the order details came to mind.

common_difficulties.description: The point is asserted with too little concrete material for the reader to accept it.
Details concern the same topic but do not develop the paragraph's actual point.
Relevant details appear in no functional order, so their cumulative effect is lost.
Details are listed without showing their relationship to the central idea.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: More detail always makes a paragraph stronger.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner values development.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Shift from quantity to function: which details does the claim actually require?

productive_misconceptions.misconception: Anything true about the topic belongs in the paragraph.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner is gathering material.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Introduce relevance-to-the-point as the test for inclusion.

indicators_of_development.early: Adds little, or piles on topic-related facts with no clear relationship to the point.
indicators_of_development.partial: Adds relevant details but leaves their connection implicit or orders them loosely; adjusts when the point's requirements are named.
indicators_of_development.independent: The student selects and organizes details according to their function rather than accumulating loosely related information.
indicators_of_development.flexible: The student selects and organizes details according to their function rather than accumulating loosely related information.

recognition_diagnostics_detailed.attempting: Is the learner developing the point or accumulating topic-related information? Quote the details.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.control_level: Are details relevant, sufficient, ordered, and tied to the central idea? Map to early/partial/independent/flexible.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.likely_misconception: Same-topic facts with no link -> irrelevant/unexplained; too little -> underdeveloped.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.next_move: Ask what the reader still needs to accept the point, then select and connect the details that supply it.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Name what the paragraph's point requires the reader to know.
Judge which existing details actually develop the point.
Order details by their function in the paragraph.
Make each detail's relationship to the central idea explicit.

followup_decisions.after: Learner improves the supporting detail in the targeted way.
followup_decisions.consider: continue — consolidate the gain, then check the next-most-limiting aspect.

followup_decisions.after: The supporting detail now works but a neighbor is the real obstacle.

followup_decisions.consider: conclude this target — consolidate and release.

Reorder details so they build toward the paragraph's contribution.
Add one sentence connecting each detail to the central idea.

Diminishing returns — the element substantially works and further tuning yields little developmental gain.
Another component has become the primary obstacle to communicating the meaning.

transfer.other_assignments: 'What does this claim require?' governs support in any developed paragraph.
transfer.other_disciplines: Discipline sets what counts as sufficient detail; the selection habit is constant.
transfer.future_writing: Foundational for developed, non-padded professional and academic paragraphs.

instructional_objects.definition: A sentence that completes a paragraph’s work and helps the reader understand its significance or connection to what follows.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Complete a paragraph's work and mark its significance or link to what follows.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Synthesize the paragraph’s contribution; state its implication; connect it to the larger claim or next idea; avoid merely repeating the topic sentence.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Does the paragraph end abruptly? Does the final sentence add significance or simply restate earlier wording? Is closure actually needed?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Ends abruptly; restates the topic sentence; unnecessary closure.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask, “What should the reader now understand because of this paragraph?” Invite the student to express that implication.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_control: The student closes paragraphs selectively and purposefully, emphasizing implications or movement in the argument.
instructional_objects.reader_function: Leaves the reader with the paragraph's significance or its link to what follows, rather than a flat stop.
instructional_objects.writer_function: Makes the writer state what the paragraph established and why it matters, testing whether the paragraph did its job.

functional_relationships.purpose: Completes the paragraph's share of the purpose; names the 'so what' of the paragraph.
functional_relationships.reader: Tells the reader what to carry forward from the paragraph.
functional_relationships.neighboring_components: Answers the Topic Sentence; bridges to the next Paragraph; contributes to overall Coherence.
functional_relationships.overall_organization: Optional by design — used where a paragraph needs closure or a hinge, not mechanically.

common_difficulties.description: Merely repeats the topic sentence wording without adding significance.
The paragraph stops without completing its point, leaving the reader unsure what it established.
Closure is forced where the paragraph's point is already complete.
Introduces a new idea instead of completing the current one.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: Every paragraph needs a concluding sentence.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: Shows attention to closure.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Move to selectivity: closure is used where it adds significance or movement, not by rule.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: A conclusion restates what was said.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner values reinforcement.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Redirect from restatement to implication: what should the reader now understand?

indicators_of_development.early: Ends abruptly or repeats the opening sentence; cannot say what the paragraph established.
indicators_of_development.partial: States an implication but it echoes earlier wording or adds a tangent; refines when asked for the 'so what'.
indicators_of_development.independent: The student closes paragraphs selectively and purposefully, emphasizing implications or movement in the argument.
indicators_of_development.flexible: The student closes paragraphs selectively and purposefully, emphasizing implications or movement in the argument.

recognition_diagnostics_detailed.attempting: Is the ending restating, completing, or wandering? Quote the final sentence.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.control_level: Does it synthesize the contribution, state an implication, or connect forward — without mere repetition? Map to levels.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.likely_misconception: Echoes the topic sentence -> restates; adds a new idea -> new_tangent.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.next_move: Ask what the reader should now understand because of the paragraph, and whether closure is even needed here.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Have the learner name what the paragraph established.
Test what the reader should carry forward.
Decide whether this paragraph needs closure at all.
Bridge the paragraph's point to the next idea.

followup_decisions.after: Learner improves the concluding sentence in the targeted way.
followup_decisions.consider: continue — consolidate the gain, then check the next-most-limiting aspect.

followup_decisions.after: Learner repeats the same difficulty after one invitation.
followup_decisions.consider: increase_support — vary the scaffold (change the lens); do NOT supply the content.

followup_decisions.after: The concluding sentence now works but a neighbor is the real obstacle.
followup_decisions.consider: change_target to Coherence — this element is no longer the bottleneck.

followup_decisions.after: Learner independently performs and can explain the change.
followup_decisions.consider: conclude this target — consolidate and release.

followup_decisions.after: Learner asks to proceed on their own.
followup_decisions.consider: stop — hand back control (independence request).

revision_strategies: Replace a restatement with the paragraph's implication ('what this means for the argument').
Add a one-clause bridge to the next paragraph where the argument needs a hinge.
Delete a forced closing sentence when the paragraph is already complete.
stopping_conditions: Learner independently produces a concluding sentence that performs its canonical function for this reader and purpose.
Diminishing returns — the element substantially works and further tuning yields little developmental gain.
Another component has become the primary obstacle to communicating the meaning.
Learner requests independence.
Teacher override designates a different focus.

transfer.other_genres: Completion-vs-stop transfers to scene endings, section wrap-ups, and stanza turns.
transfer.other_assignments: 'What should the reader carry forward?' applies to any paragraph that needs a hinge.
transfer.other_disciplines: Where each section's takeaway must be explicit (reports), the function is heightened.
transfer.future_writing: Foundational for signposted professional writing readers can follow by takeaways.

instructional_objects.definition: A group of related sentences that develops one coherent contribution to a larger piece of writing.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Develop one coherent contribution to the larger text.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Establish a central purpose or claim; orient the reader; develop the idea through explanation, evidence, and examples; organize sentences logically; connect the paragraph to the larger text.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Does the paragraph have one governing purpose? Are sentences relevant and coherently ordered? Is it adequately developed? Should it be divided or combined?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: No single governing purpose; irrelevant/disordered sentences; under- or over-developed.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask the student to state the paragraph’s job in the essay and examine how each sentence contributes to that job.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_control: The student constructs unified, developed paragraphs of flexible length and organizes them according to meaning rather than formula.
instructional_objects.reader_function: Delivers one coherent chunk of meaning the reader can take in as a unit and connect to the whole.
instructional_objects.writer_function: Requires the writer to commit a group of sentences to a single job and to build that job out.

functional_relationships.purpose: A paragraph performs one share of the whole purpose; multiple jobs signal it should be split.
functional_relationships.reader: Lets the reader absorb the argument in digestible, ordered units.
functional_relationships.neighboring_components: Built from Topic Sentence + Supporting Detail (+ Concluding Sentence); a unit of Organization.
functional_relationships.overall_organization: Paragraph breaks and order should reflect the movement of meaning, not a fixed count.

common_difficulties.description: Sentences concern a topic but no single contribution governs them.
The point is asserted without enough explanation, evidence, or example.
Relevant sentences are ordered so the reader cannot follow the development.
Two or more distinct jobs are crammed into one paragraph that should be divided.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: A paragraph must be a set number of sentences.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: Shows awareness that paragraphs have shape.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Replace length rules with function: length follows the job the paragraph must do.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: A new idea means a new paragraph, always.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner senses paragraphs track ideas.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Refine to one governing contribution: related sentences that serve one job stay together.

indicators_of_development.early: Writes topic-related sentences with no single governing purpose or clear order.
indicators_of_development.partial: Holds one purpose but under-develops or mis-orders it, or should split; reorganizes when the paragraph's job is named.
indicators_of_development.independent: The student constructs unified, developed paragraphs of flexible length and organizes them according to meaning rather than formula.
indicators_of_development.flexible: The student constructs unified, developed paragraphs of flexible length and organizes them according to meaning rather than formula.

recognition_diagnostics_detailed.attempting: Can the learner state this paragraph's single job? Quote the paragraph.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.control_level: One governing purpose? Relevant, ordered sentences? Adequately developed? Right size (split/combine)? Map to levels.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.likely_misconception: Two jobs in one -> overloaded; loose order -> incoherent_order.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.next_move: Have the learner name the paragraph's job, then test each sentence against it.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Name the paragraph's single job.
Order sentences to build the point; split overloaded paragraphs.
Develop an under-supported point.
Have the learner justify what each sentence contributes.
developmental_invitations.avoid_when: The learner is still unclear on the job.

followup_decisions.after: Learner improves the paragraph in the targeted way.
followup_decisions.consider: continue — consolidate the gain, then check the next-most-limiting aspect.

followup_decisions.after: Learner repeats the same difficulty after one invitation.
followup_decisions.consider: increase_support — vary the scaffold (change the lens); do NOT supply the content.

followup_decisions.after: The paragraph now works but a neighbor is the real obstacle.
followup_decisions.consider: change_target to Organization — this element is no longer the bottleneck.

followup_decisions.after: Learner independently performs and can explain the change.
followup_decisions.consider: conclude this target — consolidate and release.

followup_decisions.after: Learner asks to proceed on their own.
followup_decisions.consider: stop — hand back control (independence request).

revision_strategies: State the paragraph's job in one phrase, then cut or move sentences that do not serve it.
Split a paragraph that carries two jobs into two paragraphs, each with its own point.
Develop a thin paragraph with the explanation/evidence the point requires.
stopping_conditions: Learner independently produces a paragraph that performs its canonical function for this reader and purpose.
Diminishing returns — the element substantially works and further tuning yields little developmental gain.
Another component has become the primary obstacle to communicating the meaning.
Learner requests independence.
Teacher override designates a different focus.

transfer.other_assignments: 'What is this paragraph's job?' governs paragraphing in any prose.
transfer.other_disciplines: Conventions on length differ; the one-contribution principle is constant.
transfer.future_writing: Foundational for readable reports, articles, and documentation.

instructional_objects.definition: The opening section that brings readers into the subject, establishes the writing situation, and prepares them for the essay's central direction.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Bring the reader into the subject and prepare them for the central claim.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Engage attention appropriately; introduce the subject and problem; provide necessary context; establish relevance; clarify key terms when needed; lead toward the thesis or controlling purpose.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Does the reader understand the subject, stakes, and direction? Is context missing or excessive? Is the opening generic, disconnected, or overly broad?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Reader lacks subject/stakes/direction; context missing or excessive; generic or overly broad opening.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask what the intended reader must know before encountering the thesis and what would make the problem worth attending to.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_control: The student adapts introductions to audience and purpose, selects relevant context, and creates a coherent path toward the central claim.
instructional_objects.reader_function: Orients the reader to the subject, the stakes, and — above all — the DIRECTION of the essay, so they know what to expect and why it is worth reading.
instructional_objects.writer_function: Commits the writer to a destination and a reader; an introduction cannot be built well until the writer knows what the essay will establish and for whom.

functional_relationships.purpose: The introduction exists to deliver the reader to the thesis with the context and motivation needed to accept it; with no thesis/purpose, there is no destination to introduce.
functional_relationships.reader: Calibrated to what THIS reader needs before the claim — too little context loses them, too much buries the point.
functional_relationships.neighboring_components: Depends on Thesis/Purpose (the destination), Audience Awareness (how much context), and draws on Hook/Opening Move and Background/Context; it is frequently a symptom whose cause lives in those objects.
functional_relationships.overall_organization: Sets the trajectory the body will follow; a reader who finishes the intro unsure of the path signals a direction problem, not a wording problem.

common_difficulties.description: An engaging opening that never tells the reader where the essay is going.
A hook unrelated to the thesis — attention captured, then wasted.
Accurate context with no motivation or destination — an info-dump.
States the claim but gives the reader no context or stakes to receive it.
'In this essay I will...' describes the plan instead of introducing the idea.
The real opening/claim arrives only after paragraphs of warm-up.
'Since the dawn of time...' generic universals that orient no one.

instructionally_significant_discriminati.observable_performance: A vivid opening that doesn't connect to the argument.
possible_interpretations: No thesis/destination yet to connect to
Has a thesis but doesn't see the hook must serve it
Thinks a hook's job is only to be interesting
instructionally_significant_discriminati.evidence_to_distinguish: Check whether a clear thesis exists elsewhere in the draft, then ask what job the opening should do for THIS argument.

response_per_interpretation.no_thesis: Retarget upstream — establish the claim/purpose first.
response_per_interpretation.has_thesis: Connect the hook to the thesis (the opening should earn the claim).
response_per_interpretation.hook_as_decoration: Reframe the hook's purpose: orient the reader to this argument, not merely entertain.

instructionally_significant_discriminati.common_incorrect_response: Coaching hook craft when there is no thesis for the hook to serve.
instructionally_significant_discriminati.why_it_matters: Teaching a better opening is wasted if the essay has no destination; the leverage is the destination.

possible_interpretations: Missing thesis/purpose (no direction to give)
Weak audience awareness (dumping all known context)
Organizational problem (direction exists but is misplaced)
instructionally_significant_discriminati.evidence_to_distinguish: Ask what the reader most needs to know to reach the claim, and whether a claim exists yet.

response_per_interpretation.audience: Select only reader-necessary context; cut the rest.
response_per_interpretation.organization: Move the existing direction forward so background becomes purposeful.

instructionally_significant_discriminati.common_incorrect_response: Telling the learner to 'trim the background' without first establishing the direction that makes trimming meaningful.
instructionally_significant_discriminati.why_it_matters: Background is aimless until there is a destination; sequencing the fix matters.

possible_interpretations: No claim yet (announces because nothing to assert)
Has a claim but front-loads a roadmap out of habit
Genre confusion (thinks intros state plans)
instructionally_significant_discriminati.evidence_to_distinguish: Ask the learner to state the IDEA (not the plan) in one sentence; a ready idea means it's habit/genre, a blank means the claim is missing.

response_per_interpretation.roadmap_habit: Convert the plan-statement into an idea plus orientation.
response_per_interpretation.genre_confusion: Distinguish introducing an idea from announcing a plan.

instructionally_significant_discriminati.common_incorrect_response: Rewriting the announcement into a polished plan-statement, cementing the habit.
instructionally_significant_discriminati.why_it_matters: Announcements usually signal a missing claim; fixing surface wording hides the real gap.

instructional_leverage.observable_learner_state: Engaging or disconnected hook, but the reader cannot tell where the essay is going.
possible_responses: Connect the hook to the thesis/purpose
instructional_leverage.recommended_first_response: Secure the destination: make sure a clear purpose/thesis exists, then make the opening serve it.
instructional_leverage.why_highest_leverage: The introduction's core job is to orient the reader toward a destination; a clever opening that leads nowhere cannot be improved by more polish. Direction unlocks every other opening decision.
instructional_leverage.when_another_takes_priority: If NO thesis exists yet -> fix the thesis first (dependency). If a strong thesis already exists and only the hook is off -> connecting/replacing the hook is the move.

instructional_leverage.observable_learner_state: Accurate background with no motivation or direction (info-dump).
instructional_leverage.recommended_first_response: Surface the direction and the stakes (why it matters), so the background becomes selectable against a destination.
instructional_leverage.why_highest_leverage: Background gains meaning only from direction; establishing 'where and why' lets the learner see which context is relevant and cut the rest — a durable, transferable move.
instructional_leverage.when_another_takes_priority: If the claim/purpose is missing -> thesis first. If the context is simply irrelevant -> cut before reorganizing.

instructional_leverage.observable_learner_state: Reader is confused about the paper's trajectory even though content is present.
instructional_leverage.recommended_first_response: Make the destination visible early — ensure the thesis's direction is clear, then order the opening to lead there.
instructional_leverage.why_highest_leverage: Reader orientation IS the introduction's function; clarity of trajectory matters more than elegance and is what a reader actually needs.
instructional_leverage.when_another_takes_priority: If the confusion stems from an unfocused thesis -> thesis precision first (a forecasting sentence cannot forecast an unclear claim).

instructional_leverage.observable_learner_state: Opening is competent but flat; the learner wants it to be 'better'.
possible_responses: Leave it and move to the body
instructional_leverage.recommended_first_response: Check leverage before investing: if the opening already orients the reader and leads to the thesis, move to higher-leverage work (evidence, reasoning, organization).
instructional_leverage.why_highest_leverage: Polishing an already-functional introduction is low developmental return; the learner grows more by working where the reader is actually being lost.
instructional_leverage.when_another_takes_priority: If the assignment/genre foregrounds engagement (e.g., a personal or persuasive piece) and the flat opening genuinely disengages the reader -> then invest in stakes/hook.

instructional_objects.leverage_over_correctness_note: A technically better introduction is not always the best next move. If the learner lacks a clear purpose, a sense of the reader, organization, or confidence, address that first — a polished opening built on an unclear destination does not help the writer develop.

cross_object_dependencies.action: If no clear destination exists, retarget to Thesis/Purpose before shaping the opening.
Establish direction (or reorder) before trimming context.
Elicit the idea; if none, retarget to Thesis.

cross_object_dependencies.intro_symptom: cannot judge which context is relevant
cross_object_dependencies.action: Address audience awareness; if the learner lacks the content itself, the Knowledge Loop (Orientation) precedes intro work.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: An introduction's job is to grab attention.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner cares about the reader's engagement.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Extend 'grab attention' to 'orient the reader toward the point' — attention in service of direction.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: Start broad ('Since the beginning of time') then narrow.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner senses an intro should set a stage.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Replace the empty universal with the specific problem THIS reader needs to care about.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: Tell the reader your plan so they know what's coming.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner values orientation.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Convert the plan-statement into the idea itself plus a real sense of direction.

indicators_of_development.early: Opens with a generic or disconnected move; states a plan rather than an idea; gives the reader no clear direction.
indicators_of_development.partial: Provides some orientation but misjudges context (too much/little) or lets the hook drift from the thesis; fixes it when pointed out.
indicators_of_development.independent: Independently orients the reader, selects relevant context, and leads coherently to the thesis.
indicators_of_development.flexible: Adapts the opening to genre, audience, and purpose; calibrates engagement and context to what the specific reader needs.

recognition_diagnostics_detailed.attempting: Identify what the opening is doing — hooking, giving background, announcing, or orienting — and whether a destination (thesis) is visible.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.control_level: Does the reader end the intro knowing the subject, the stakes, and the direction? Is context reader-necessary? Map to early/partial/independent/flexible.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.likely_misconception: See instructionally_significant_discriminations; then check cross_object_dependencies before teaching intro craft.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.next_move: Run the destination check first; if the destination is missing/unclear, retarget upstream; otherwise choose the leverage-ranked intro move.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Make the essay's direction clear early.
developmental_invitations.use_when: The reader can't tell where the paper is going.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Establish why the subject matters to this reader.
developmental_invitations.use_when: Background is aimless or the opening is flat.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Tie an engaging opening to the thesis.
developmental_invitations.use_when: A hook exists but is disconnected.
developmental_invitations.avoid_when: There is no thesis to connect to yet (retarget).

developmental_invitations.purpose: Keep only the context the reader needs to reach the claim.
developmental_invitations.avoid_when: Context is already lean and relevant.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Signal the trajectory without listing a plan.
developmental_invitations.use_when: Reader is unsure of the path but the thesis is clear.
developmental_invitations.avoid_when: The thesis itself is unclear (sharpen it first).

developmental_invitations.purpose: Turn 'I will discuss...' into the idea itself.
developmental_invitations.avoid_when: No claim exists yet (retarget to Thesis).

developmental_invitations.purpose: Have the learner predict what a reader expects after the intro.
Have the learner state what their introduction promises the reader.
developmental_invitations.avoid_when: The intro is not yet oriented.

followup_decisions.after: Destination check shows NO clear thesis.
followup_decisions.consider: change_target to Thesis/Purpose before any intro work.

followup_decisions.after: Thesis is clear; hook is disconnected.
followup_decisions.consider: continue — connect_hook_to_purpose.

followup_decisions.after: Learner adds direction and stakes to background.
followup_decisions.consider: continue — select_relevant_context, then move on.

followup_decisions.after: Intro now orients the reader and leads to the thesis.
followup_decisions.consider: conclude this target; move to higher-leverage body work.

followup_decisions.after: Confusion traces to an unfocused thesis.
followup_decisions.consider: change_target to Thesis precision.

followup_decisions.after: Learner cannot supply needed context (lacks the knowledge).
followup_decisions.consider: route to the Knowledge Loop (Orientation) before continuing.

revision_strategies: Add or surface the direction early so the reader knows the destination.
Replace a generic/universal opening with the specific problem the reader should care about.
Connect or replace a disconnected hook so it earns the thesis.
Cut context the reader does not need to reach the claim; keep what they do.
Convert an 'I will discuss...' announcement into the idea itself plus orientation.
Move a buried opening/claim to the front so the essay's path is visible.
stopping_conditions: Learner independently orients the reader, selects relevant context, and leads to the thesis.
Diminishing returns — the introduction does its job for the intended reader.
The real bottleneck is upstream (thesis/purpose) or content (knowledge) -> retarget.
Learner requests independence; or teacher override designates another focus.

genre_variation.argument_persuasive: Foreground the stakes and the contested question; a motivating problem earns the claim.
genre_variation.explanatory: Foreground the subject and why it is worth understanding; orient before explaining.
genre_variation.literary_analysis: Foreground the interpretive question about the text; minimal plot summary, quick move to the claim.
genre_variation.historical: Foreground the situation and its significance; supply only orienting context, not a full chronicle.
genre_variation.scientific: Foreground the question/problem and its relevance; context is background to the investigation.
genre_variation.personal_reflective: Engagement and voice carry more weight; a scene or tension may legitimately open the piece.

transfer.other_genres: The orient-the-reader-toward-a-destination function is constant; the balance of hook, context, and stakes varies by genre.
transfer.other_assignments: The habit of asking 'what does my reader need before my main point, and do they know where I'm going?' applies to any piece.
transfer.other_disciplines: Orienting context differs by field, but every discipline expects a reader to know the question and its significance up front.
transfer.future_writing: Foundational for reports, proposals, emails, and any communication where a reader decides quickly whether to keep reading.

instructional_objects.definition: An opening that gives the reader a meaningful reason to attend to the subject.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Give the reader a genuine, relevant reason to care about the subject.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Identify what is interesting, puzzling, consequential, vivid, or contested about the subject; present it accurately; connect it directly to the essay’s purpose.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Does the opening create relevant interest or merely use a decorative question, quotation, or dramatic statement? Is its connection to the essay clear?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Decorative/generic hook; unclear connection to the essay.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask what is genuinely surprising, important, or unresolved about the topic and help the student begin there.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_control: The student creates varied, relevant openings and abandons formulaic hooks that do not serve the essay.
instructional_objects.reader_function: Gives the reader a genuine reason to care about the subject from the first lines.
instructional_objects.writer_function: Makes the writer locate what is actually compelling about the subject rather than decorate the opening.

functional_relationships.purpose: The opening must serve the essay's purpose, not merely attract attention.
functional_relationships.reader: Creates relevant interest tied to what the essay will do.
functional_relationships.neighboring_components: Part of the Introduction; leads toward Background/Context and the Thesis.
functional_relationships.overall_organization: Sets the entry point; its promise must be paid off by the essay.

common_difficulties.description: A generic question, quotation, or dramatic line that does not connect to the essay's purpose.
Interest is created but its link to the essay is unclear.
Opens with sweeping generality ('Since the dawn of time') rather than the real subject.
Promises a subject or tone the essay does not deliver.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: An essay must start with a hook.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: Shows awareness that openings should engage.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Move from a required device to a relevant reason: what is genuinely worth attending to here?

productive_misconceptions.misconception: A surprising fact or quote is automatically a good hook.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner is reaching for interest.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Test the device against purpose: does it lead into what the essay argues?

indicators_of_development.early: Opens with a formula (broad statement, generic question) unrelated to the essay's real point.
indicators_of_development.partial: Creates interest but its connection to the essay's purpose is loose; sharpens when asked what is truly at stake.
indicators_of_development.independent: The student creates varied, relevant openings and abandons formulaic hooks that do not serve the essay.
indicators_of_development.flexible: The student creates varied, relevant openings and abandons formulaic hooks that do not serve the essay.

recognition_diagnostics_detailed.attempting: Is the opening decorative or purpose-connected? Quote it.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.control_level: Does it create RELEVANT interest and connect clearly to the essay's purpose? Map to levels.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.likely_misconception: Generic device -> decorative; sweeping start -> overbroad.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.next_move: Ask what is genuinely surprising, important, or unresolved about the topic and start there.

developmental_invitations.purpose: Find what is actually compelling about the subject.

instructional_objects.definition: The purposeful reworking of writing to improve what it communicates and how effectively it does so.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Rework writing to better serve purpose, meaning, structure, and reader.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Reconsider purpose and task; evaluate reader understanding; examine global organization and central claims; revise paragraphs and reasoning; refine sentences and words; proofread after substantive changes.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Is revision limited to correction and word substitution? Does the student recognize mismatches among purpose, meaning, structure, and reader response?

instructional_objects.reader_function: Improves what the writing communicates and how well, judged by a reader's actual understanding.
instructional_objects.writer_function: Makes the writer re-see the draft against purpose, meaning, and reader response — not just fix errors.

functional_relationships.overall_organization: Substantive changes precede proofreading; global before local.

Sentences are polished while larger problems remain.

productive_misconceptions.leverage: Expand to substance: revision reworks meaning and structure, then proofreads.

productive_misconceptions.leverage: Introduce the reader's perspective as the test.

indicators_of_development.flexible: The student rereads from a reader’s perspective, identifies consequential problems, makes substantive changes, and explains why revisions improve the writing.

instructional_objects.definition: An explanation of what a word, idea, or concept means in the present context.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Make an important concept understandable to the intended reader.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: State the concept’s basic meaning; identify its defining qualities; explain unfamiliar words within the explanation; distinguish it from related concepts when useful; elaborate until the intended reader can understand it.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Is an important concept unexplained? Would the intended reader understand the explanation? Is it circular, vague, overly broad, overly narrow, or merely an example?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Important concept left unexplained; circular/vague/over-broad/over-narrow; example given instead of definition.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask the student to explain the concept in ordinary language. Identify one unclear word or idea in that explanation and invite further elaboration.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_control: The student recognizes when a concept requires explanation and constructs appropriately complete definitions for different audiences and purposes.
instructional_objects.reader_function: Gives the reader a shared, sufficient understanding of a term before it does work in the argument.
instructional_objects.writer_function: Forces the writer to make a concept's meaning explicit and complete enough for this reader and purpose.

functional_relationships.purpose: A definition serves the argument by making a load-bearing term mean the same thing for writer and reader.
functional_relationships.reader: Supplies the meaning the reader needs; tested by whether the intended reader would understand it.
functional_relationships.neighboring_components: Grounds the Concept it names; supports Central Claim/Thesis when a key term is contested.
functional_relationships.overall_organization: Placed where the term first does work; elaborated only as far as the reader needs.

common_difficulties.description: Defines the term using the term itself.
Too general to fix the meaning for this reader.
Includes too much or too little to match the intended meaning.
Offers an instance in place of the general meaning.

productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner values precision and authority.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Move to context: the definition must fit how the term is used in THIS argument.

productive_misconceptions.misconception: Only hard words need defining.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner senses definitions clarify.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Shift to load-bearing terms: define what the argument depends on, familiar or not.

indicators_of_development.early: Uses a term without explaining it, or defines it circularly/by example.
indicators_of_development.partial: Explains the term but too vaguely or broadly for the reader; sharpens when one unclear word is probed.
indicators_of_development.independent: The student recognizes when a concept requires explanation and constructs appropriately complete definitions for different audiences and purposes.
indicators_of_development.flexible: The student recognizes when a concept requires explanation and constructs appropriately complete definitions for different audiences and purposes.

recognition_diagnostics_detailed.likely_misconception: Term-in-its-own-definition -> circular; instance offered -> example_for_definition.
recognition_diagnostics_detailed.next_move: Ask the learner to explain the concept in ordinary language, then probe one unclear word for elaboration.

developmental_invitations.use_when: The definition is vague or circular.
developmental_invitations.avoid_when: Meaning is already clear to the reader.

instructional_objects.definition: A general idea used to organize and interpret particular examples, experiences, or events.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Give the reader an organizing idea that governs particular cases.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Name the idea; identify the qualities that make something an instance of it; distinguish central from incidental features; connect examples to the general idea; clarify its boundaries.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: Is the student using a term without understanding it? Are examples confused with the concept? Are defining qualities missing or inconsistent?
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Term used without understanding; examples confused with the concept; inconsistent defining qualities.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask what different examples have in common and what would not count as an example. Help the student state the general idea.

instructional_objects.writer_function: Requires the writer to hold an abstraction steadily — its defining features and its boundaries.

functional_relationships.purpose: Concepts let the argument generalize; the purpose determines which concept is doing the organizing.
functional_relationships.reader: Lets the reader see what unites the particulars and what would not count.
functional_relationships.neighboring_components: Named by a Definition; instantiated by Examples; organizes Classification.
functional_relationships.overall_organization: Governs how particulars are grouped and interpreted across the piece.

Treats a single instance as the general idea.
The qualities that define the concept shift from case to case.
No sense of what would NOT count as an instance.

productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner reasons from concrete cases.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Lift to the general: what do the examples share that makes them instances?

productive_misconceptions.misconception: If I can name it, I understand it.
productive_misconceptions.why_productive: The learner has the vocabulary.
productive_misconceptions.leverage: Test understanding by boundaries: what would not count?

indicators_of_development.partial: States the general idea but its defining features waver or its boundaries are unclear; steadies when tested with non-instances.
indicators_of_development.independent: The student explains concepts abstractly, identifies valid and invalid examples, and uses concepts consistently in new contexts.
indicators_of_development.flexible: The student explains concepts abstractly, identifies valid and invalid examples, and uses concepts consistently in new contexts.

instructional_objects.definition: Showing the reader how several developed ideas fit together into a larger point.
instructional_objects.communicative_purpose: Show how multiple ideas work together to create a meaning larger than any one of them alone.
instructional_objects.performance_structure: Gather the developed ideas that belong together; name the relationship among them; state the larger point that emerges from combining them; show the reader why the whole means more than the parts.
instructional_objects.recognition_diagnostics: The draft lists or explains several ideas but never states what they add up to; the reader is left to assemble the larger meaning alone.
instructional_objects.common_obstacles: Mere summary instead of integration; disconnected points left side by side; restating each idea without naming the larger point they create together.
instructional_objects.next_developmental_moves: Ask the student which ideas belong together and what larger point those ideas make when combined; invite them to write the one sentence that states the meaning created by the combination.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_control: The student independently draws developed ideas together into a stated larger meaning, rather than summarizing them one by one.

functional_relationships.explanation: Synthesis builds on ideas the student has already explained; it names what those explanations add up to.
functional_relationships.organization: Synthesis depends on the ideas being developed and arranged clearly enough to be combined.
functional_relationships.conclusion: Synthesis often prepares closure by establishing the larger meaning the ending completes.

revision_strategies: Underline the separate ideas, then write one sentence stating what they mean together.
Replace a summary sentence with a sentence that names the relationship among the ideas.
instructional_objects.indicators_of_development: Begins to state a combined meaning rather than re-listing ideas.
stopping_conditions: Learner independently states the larger meaning created by combining developed ideas.
Diminishing returns — the element performs its canonical function for this reader and purpose.
